_comment: Sample posts for the PREVIEW layout only (dist/preview.html). Not injected into the main console yet. Prose is original — paraphrase and cite the books, never paste them. Voice: Bill, first person, conversational.

posts.title: If you're reading this, SCUT still works
posts.dek: Public features include several blogs. This is one of them, or a mock-up of one, depending how pedantic you're feeling.
posts.body:
Garfield keeps telling me nobody reads these. He also keeps opening them, so the data is mixed.

This feed is where status used to go before status became seventeen competing channels and a moot invite. Genealogy work still lives in the registry — separate tool, same network. If the tabs feel crowded, that is not a metaphor. We have a lot of tabs.

Ping me if something in the tree looks wrong. Bring a citation. "I think I remember" is how we got Loki under the wrong parent for a while, and I would rather not do that again.

posts.title: Read the back of the book
posts.dek: There is a genealogy printed in the novel. There is also a PDF on the open net. They do not always agree, and only one of them is Taylor.
posts.body:
We spent a long time treating an online tree as if it were load-bearing. Then somebody finally read the appendices — Cast of Characters, Genealogy, the works — and eighteen parentages moved from "maybe" to "on the page."

Spelling is not a side quest. Jonny and Jacques are written one way in the book and another way in the secondary tree. The book wins. That is the whole epistemology of this project in two sentences.

If you are building your own chart at home: point at a chapter, or admit you cannot. The registry will not draw an edge to be polite.

posts.title: A word that looks like a name usually isn't
posts.dek: Bestiary false positives: field notes from the purge.
posts.body:
Candidate lists lie. "Landers" is a person. "Spits" is an island faction. "Boojums" are drones. "Hexghi" is family structure. File any of those under fauna and the console starts arguing the opposite of the books.

We also almost missed dragons, which is embarrassing at a hundred-plus mentions.

Rule that stays: a name is people or fauna, never both. The build checks. I am not above being saved from myself by a script.
